subject: Clarifying SOC 2 applicability across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments
summary: FinTechCo requested confirmation of which Redwood deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC/on-prem) are covered by Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report and whether a bridge letter can cover the period between audits. Internal compliance clarified control plane vs data plane inclusion and provided artifacts and a bridge letter. Final confirmation received.
messages:
From: Amrinder Singh <amrinder.s@fintechco.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTechCo Security <security@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — appreciate the time. Our security team is reviewing Redwood as part of a procurement review. Two quick asks before we can move to procurement: 1) Please confirm whether Redwood's SOC 2 Type II (latest report) covers hosted API customers and Dedicated tenants by default, and 2) if Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments are covered or require a separate attestation/contractual addendum.

Also, what's your current audit period (start/end dates) for the Type II report, and do you provide a bridge letter if our go-live falls outside the audit window?

If useful, attach whichever artifacts you can share (report, bridge letter). We need this for our vendor risk questionnaire.

Best,
Amrinder
Security Lead, FinTechCo
[FinTechCo PGP: available on request]

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amrinder Singh <amrinder.s@fintechco.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Amrinder — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Mina (Compliance) and Laura (Sales Ops) so we can get an authoritative answer and artifacts.

Quick note while we pull docs: Redwood's published SOC 2 Type II report covers our Hosted API and the Redwood-managed control plane that powers all deployments. Dedicated (reserved capacity) customers using Redwood Dedicated are covered for the managed portions of the service (control plane, provisioning, multi-tenant control services) but there are caveats for network isolation and customer-managed infrastructure — Mina will clarify. Private/on-prem deployments often fall outside the standard report scope because the customer controls the data plane; in some cases we provide a tailored attestation or an MSA addendum.

We will follow up with the report, a deployment matrix, and a bridge-letter template.

Thanks,
Sooj
Soojín Lee | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Amrinder Singh <amrinder.s@fintechco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Amrinder,

Thanks for the questions — attaching the redacted SOC 2 Type II report (see attachment) and the deployment matrix (deployment-matrix-redwood.xlsx) that maps our control applicability across deployment modes. Short answers:

- Audit period for the attached Type II report: 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31.
- Coverage: Hosted API (all control domains in the report) — fully covered.
- Dedicated: The report covers Redwood-managed control domains (control plane, access management, deployment orchestration, and monitoring) but does not assert control over customer-managed networking or customer-provided HW in Dedicated configurations. The deployment matrix shows which control activities are shared vs customer responsibility.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: These are typically out of scope for the standard Type II because the customer controls the data plane. For VPC Private deployments where Redwood still manages the control plane in the customer's VPC, we can include certain control domains; for fully on-prem air-gapped installs, we provide evidence packages and can negotiate a scoped attestation or SOC addendum per contract.

Bridge letters: We do provide a signed bridge letter to cover the period from the end of the last audit through January 31, 2026 for customers in active negotiations. Attached is our standard bridge letter template (SOC2_Bridge_Letter_Jan2026.pdf) — we can customize dates/customer references as needed.

Action items:
- Please confirm whether FinTechCo will be Hosted, Dedicated (Redwood-managed HW), Dedicated (customer-provided HW), or Private/on-prem so we can mark the shared/responsible controls.
- If you want the bridge letter finalized, provide the legal entity name and target go-live date.

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_2025_Redwood_Inference.pdf (redacted), deployment-matrix-redwood.xlsx, SOC2_Bridge_Letter_Jan2026.pdf

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Amrinder Singh <amrinder.s@fintechco.com>

Cc: FinTechCo Security <security@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Thanks Mina. We're evaluating two configurations in parallel: 1) Hosted (fastest) and 2) Dedicated on customer-controlled hardware (we will colocate our instances but Redwood will manage the control plane/orchestration software). For the Dedicated-on-customer-hardware option: can you confirm whether the SOC 2 report's control tests (e.g., change management, monitoring, incident response) that Redwood performs for Dedicated tenants will still be included in the report when the underlying hardware is customer-owned? We need to know if the vendor risk team must require additional attestations for customer-HW Dedicated deployments.

Also, can the bridge letter reference our company name and a planned go-live of 2026-03-15? That would bridge the gap from the audit end date through our target launch.

Regards,
Amrinder

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Amrinder Singh <amrinder.s@fintechco.com>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Amrinder — quick technical clarification from infra/ops perspective: when customers provide HW for Dedicated, Redwood still controls the software stack we deploy (inference runtime, orchestration, monitoring agents) and we perform the same change-control and incident response processes for that software stack. The primary difference is that physical security and certain platform-level network controls are customer responsibilities. Practically, our SOC control tests that depend on software/process ownership remain applicable; tests depending on ownership of physical HW or customer-managed networking are scoped out.

In short: for Dedicated-on-customer-HW where Redwood manages the software/control plane, many of our SOC 2 control activities remain valid and can be evidence-backed in the standard report scope. We recommend marking physical and network controls as customer responsibilities in the shared-responsibility matrix.

I can produce a short addendum note that explicitly lists which control IDs are still owned by Redwood in customer-HW Dedicated configs if that helps your vendor risk questionnaire.

- Dev (Infra/Operations)
